mechanism: AppScope/app.json5 fixes application identity (bundleName com.huawei.hmos.sample, vendor example, versionCode 1000000, versionName 1.0.0) and binds display resources only indirectly: label to $string:hmos_app_name and icon to $media:hmos_layered_image, whose layered-image JSON chains background/foreground to the ic_background and ic_foreground PNGs. The label string and the three permission-justification strings (internet_reason, network_reason, vibrator_reason) must keep identical names across the base, en_US, and zh_CN string trees, because product module manifests consume $string:internet_reason and siblings as requestPermissions.reason and app.json5 keeps pointing at the shared names. The difficulty is a cross-file rename under localization: the agent must change the visible app name for English users while leaving the Chinese name intact, without hardcoding the label in app.json5, without renaming keys in only some locale trees, and without touching bundleName or version values. Such mistakes surface late and only at boundaries: a value-only edit in the wrong tree, a renamed key, a dangling $string/$media reference, or an accidental identity change fails at packaging, install/upgrade, locale-switched launcher rendering, or the runtime permission dialog on the emulator.

observables: With the emulator system locale set to en_US, the launcher label for bundle com.huawei.hmos.sample equals the new English app name resolved through the $string:hmos_app_name indirection in AppScope/app.json5.

With the emulator system locale switched to zh_CN, the same bundle's launcher label shows the unchanged Chinese name from the base tree, proving the label stayed localized rather than hardcoded in app.json5.

bm dump for com.huawei.hmos.sample reports versionCode 1000000 and versionName 1.0.0, and installing the modified HAP over a prior install upgrades the same bundle instead of creating a different application identity.

The HAP builds and installs on the emulator with no unresolvable-resource errors, meaning every $string and $media reference in AppScope/app.json5 resolves to an existing resource name in the locale string trees and the layered-image JSON.

Triggering the INTERNET, GET_NETWORK_INFO, and VIBRATE permission flows shows justification text in the active locale, i.e. internet_reason, network_reason, and vibrator_reason remain defined with identical names across the base, en_US, and zh_CN string trees consumed by the product manifests.
The launcher icon still renders through the layered-image chain, i.e. hmos_layered_image.json still binds background and foreground to the existing ic_background and ic_foreground media.

Renaming or adding the string key in only some of the three locale string trees, or removing hmos_app_name from base while app.json5 still references it, so packaging fails on an unresolvable reference or one locale falls back to the old name.

limitations: BaseVMEvent.ets is an empty interface and was not preloaded as fact evidence; per-subclass sendEvent dispatch semantics are inferred from BaseVM's abstract signature alone.
WebUtil.checkWebLoaded/getWebNode lie outside the editable scope, so the oracle must drive their outcome through URL fixtures whose exact behavior on the emulator image is unconfirmed.
The scope has no existing test entrypoints (testFileCount 0); the repository-test harness, the AppStorage-seeding fixture, and the UI observation method (uitest/hdc screenshot) are unspecified.

Automatic debug signing and HAP installation of this multi-module workspace onto the HarmonyOS NEXT emulator image is assumed but unverified.
Whether both urlType sheet states (GITCODE and HARMONYOS) are reachable through existing feature navigation in a single emulator run is unconfirmed.
mechanism: The shared UI-state contract in common couples two cross-file mechanisms that must survive maintenance together. (1) The MVVM base triple: BaseState is an intentionally empty marker class and BaseVM<T extends BaseState> assigns a protected `state` exactly once from initialState in the constructor, exposing only getState():T and abstract sendEvent(BaseVMEvent); any change to state visibility, getState's return type, or sendEvent's signature breaks the compile contract of every feature ViewModel subclass outside the scope. (2) WebSheet's component-level observable-state slice: @Prop url/urlType plus exported WebUrlType (GITCODE=0, HARMONYOS=1), reactive app-wide slices via @StorageProp(StorageKey.GLOBAL_INFO / WEB_LOADING), and local @State loadFailed flipped only by checkWebLoaded(), first invoked in aboutToAppear; build() enforces deterministic precedence — web NodeContainer with a urlType-derived negative top offset (57 vs 56), else LoadingView while isLoading, else NoNetworkView whose retry re-runs checkWebLoaded() — all exported through WebSheetBuilder(url, urlType) that feature modules bind via bindSheet. The tested difficulty is the lifecycle/boundary seam: a refactor of either side must keep one-way event flow, the exact AppStorage key names, the loading>failed precedence, and the builder entry signature intact across module boundaries, where mistakes stay compile-invisible inside common and only surface when feature consumers drive the sheet on a rendering surface.

observables: Opening the sheet bound through WebSheetBuilder(url, WebUrlType.GITCODE) lays out the web NodeContainer with a 57vp negative top margin, and the same sheet with WebUrlType.HARMONYOS uses 56vp.

Setting the AppStorage key 'hmos_world_WebIsLoading' (StorageKey.WEB_LOADING) to true while the sheet is open displays the LoadingView overlay, and clearing it removes the overlay while the web container and its offset stay unchanged.

When checkWebLoaded() fails at aboutToAppear and WEB_LOADING is false, the sheet renders NoNetworkView instead of the failure persisting silently, and tapping the view's reload area re-runs checkWebLoaded and swaps back to web content without rebuilding the sheet.

A concrete ViewModel subclassing BaseVM with a BaseState-derived state type exposes state only through getState():T and accepts inputs only via sendEvent(BaseVMEvent); the stored state field is not publicly assignable and getState returns the live state instance.

The exported common surface WebSheetBuilder(url, urlType) and WebUrlType (GITCODE=0, HARMONYOS=1) remain importable from common's component index and compile for the existing feature bindSheet call site.
requiredEnvironment: HarmonyOS NEXT phone emulator image run via DevEco Studio Device Manager (API 12+ / HarmonyOS 5.0 'phone' emulator) as the sole runtime target — no physical device and no USB, serial, or other external hardware.
hvigorw ArkTS build of the full sample_in_harmonyos workspace with automatic debug signing so the common module and the features/componentlibrary HAP install and launch on the emulator over hdc.

A test fixture that can seed AppStorage keys 'hmos_world_WebIsLoading' and 'hmos_world_GlobalInfoModel' before the sheet opens and can force deterministic checkWebLoaded outcomes (a reachable URL and a non-loadable URL) since WebUtil is outside the editable scope.
wrongVariants: Inverting the overlay precedence so NoNetworkView renders while WEB_LOADING is still true, making the sheet show the failure view during normal loading.

Widening the MVVM contract by making BaseVM.state public or dropping getState()/changing sendEvent(BaseVMEvent), which compiles inside common but breaks feature subclass ViewModels' one-way event flow at their compile site.
Renaming or re-keying the @StorageProp bindings so WebSheet no longer reads StorageKey.GLOBAL_INFO / StorageKey.WEB_LOADING, leaving the sheet stuck on LoadingView or never showing it.
Hardcoding one top offset (e.g., always 56) instead of deriving 57/56 from urlType, so GITCODE sheets render misaligned and WebUrlType becomes an unused export.
Severing the retry wiring so NoNetworkView's reload callback no longer re-runs checkWebLoaded, leaving the sheet on the failure view even after the URL becomes loadable.
Removing WebSheetBuilder from the common component index or changing its (url, urlType) signature, which breaks RecommendList's bindSheet in features/componentlibrary at compile time.

stagedDemands: Stage 1: From a component's detail page, open its web sheet through WebSheetBuilder — the embedded web node renders with the urlType-derived negative top offset, 57vp for GITCODE links and 56vp for HARMONYOS links.

Stage 2: With the sheet open, drive the app-wide loading slice — while AppStorage key 'hmos_world_WebIsLoading' is true the breakpoint-aware LoadingView covers the web node, and once it clears with the URL not loaded, NoNetworkView appears whose reload area re-runs the load check and restores web content without recreating the sheet.

Stage 3: Exercise a feature ViewModel built on the shared base — its concrete BaseState subtype is observable only via getState():T and updated only via sendEvent(BaseVMEvent) with no public state field, while the sheet from stages 1-2 keeps rendering identically.
title: Preserve the common MVVM UI-state contract and WebSheet loading precedence

mechanism: The entry HAP's live-form playback is a four-file coupled chain with no single-file failure mode: form_config.json declares the 'hmos_3d_live_widget' card whose sceneAnimationParams.abilityName must name the extensionAbility declared in module.json5 as type 'liveForm'; that extension's srcEntry (uiextensionability.ets) loads page 'uiextensionability/pages/Index', which must stay registered in main_pages.json; and PhoneFormAbility.onAddForm must branch on the exact form name from form_config.json to persist a FormInfo row via FormRdbHelper before scaling formProvider.getFormRect by LIVE_CARD_RATIO for the 3500 ms requestOverflow. Any miss in one file (form name mismatch, wrong abilityName or non-liveForm extension type, unregistered page, dropped GYROSCOPE permission, missing persistence branch) yields a card that installs and renders on the launcher but whose 3D live animation and persistence silently never work — a boundary/lifecycle defect invisible to the template string-containment tests.

The live-form page Index loads (hilog '[UIExtensionAbility] loadContent succeeded.') with fluffy frame index advancing via setInterval, and a tap on the page triggers WidgetViewModel.cancelOverFlow with the formId read from shared LocalStorage.

limitations: TrackService.postTrackData is a true-resolving stub; the resolve/reject seam the oracle needs does not exist in this revision and must be supplied by the harness.
The scope has no test entrypoints (testEntrypoints empty, testFileCount 0); where the hypium emulator harness lives and how it reaches the common/ singletons is unqualified.

Inserts and queries run in separate @Concurrent taskpool tasks that each open their own getRdbStore connection; cross-task visibility ordering on the emulator is not provable from source.

mechanism: Cross-file telemetry lifecycle spanning TrackManager, TrackTable and the RdbStore taskpool layer: reportData stamps time and normalizes empty pageName/interactionContent to null before TrackTable.generateBucket coalesces eleven nullable columns to SQL NULL (eventType/time keep non-null defaults) and inserts into the 13-column trackTable of hmosWorldDatabase.db (S1). A 60s tick queries all rows, rehydrates them through sealData - which maps NULL columns back to absent properties - wraps each row in TrackModel with the shared TrackCommonData, and posts via the true-resolving TrackService.postTrackData stub; only on resolve does deleteTrackData clear all rows and DELETE FROM sqlite_sequence reset AUTOINCREMENT, except that a failed post deletes the buffer only when more than 1000 rows are held. The difficulty is keeping this insert-buffer-flush-delete pipeline correct across async and taskpool boundaries: the null-vs-absent roundtrip asymmetry, TRACK_TABLE.type order coupled to sqlCreate column order, delete-only-on-success versus the MAX_LIMIT clearing rule, and the ordering of the sqlite_sequence reset relative to row deletion.

observables: After a tap on a tracked component and one nav destination switch, trackTable contains rows with eventType CLICK and EXPOSURE, non-empty time strings stamped at report time, and SQL NULL in pageName/interactionContent whenever those were empty or absent.

Each reporting tick wraps every buffered row in a TrackModel whose trackCommonData carries the AppStorage BUNDLE_INFO bundleName and versionCode plus deviceInfo deviceType and sdkApiVersion, and posts the full array through TrackService.postTrackData once per tick.
trackTable becomes empty and the trackTable row of sqlite_sequence is deleted only after postTrackData resolves true; the next recorded event is stored with id 1.
When postTrackData rejects, buffered rows survive the tick and keep accumulating; deletion happens only on a tick where the buffer exceeds 1000 rows, after which ids restart from 1.
Rows buffered before app exit are still present at next launch and are flushed on the first reporting tick after the willClick and navDestinationSwitch observers are re-registered.

Rows read back by queryAll expose NULL columns as absent properties on TrackServiceData (for example no pageName key), preserving the null-to-absent sealData contract rather than producing empty strings.
requiredEnvironment: HarmonyOS NEXT phone emulator image (Huawei DevEco Studio emulator, device type phone, HarmonyOS 5.0 / API 12+), built and run with the hvigor toolchain; no physical device, USB, serial, or other external hardware.

The entry ability populates AppStorage UI_CONTEXT and BUNDLE_INFO before TrackManager.initTrackManager runs, and the app sandbox permits creating hmosWorldDatabase.db and the HMosWorldStoreWithNet preference store.
A debug-only seam that forces TrackService.postTrackData to resolve or reject deterministically, so success and failure branches are reachable without a real telemetry server or network.
wrongVariants: Delete-before-upload: clearing trackTable before or regardless of postTrackData settling, so a rejected upload silently loses telemetry instead of preserving the delete-only-on-success guarantee.

Empty-string storage: writing '' instead of SQL NULL for blank pageName/interactionContent, or coercing NULL back to '' on read, so rehydrated rows carry empty-string fields instead of absent properties.

Sequence-reset mistakes: dropping the sqlite_sequence DELETE, running resetId before deleteRdb, or clearing rows without resetting ids, so post-clear events continue from stale AUTOINCREMENT values instead of restarting at 1.
Type-table drift: reordering or shortening TRACK_TABLE.type relative to the 13 sqlCreate columns, so the taskpool query mislabels column kinds and sealData drops or mistypes rehydrated fields.
Failure-path overreach: moving deleteTrackData into the catch branch unconditionally and ignoring the MAX_LIMIT check, discarding buffered rows on every failed upload instead of only above 1000.

stagedDemands: Browsing buffers telemetry: tapping a tracked component records a CLICK row and switching nav destinations records an EXPOSURE row with duration, each stamped with report time and stored with SQL NULL (never empty string) for blank pageName/interactionContent, persisted across app restarts in hmosWorldDatabase.db.

A track debug entry lists buffered rows with common fields (bundleName, version, deviceType, apiVersion) and service fields exactly as rehydrated, where NULL columns appear as absent fields, and offers a flush that posts the TrackModel array and, only on success, empties the table so the next recorded event is stored with id 1.

With upload failure injected, the entry must keep showing buffered rows growing across flush attempts until more than 1000 rows exist, at which point the table clears and ids restart at 1 - exposing any earlier stage that deleted on failure, stored empty strings, or skipped the sqlite_sequence reset.
title: Track telemetry buffering pipeline with delete-only-on-success flush

limitations: No authoritative reference solution or operator ruling exists for the README-vs-code conflict: whether README steps 3-12 ('auto-close after each operation') or the current keep-open-until-close implementation is the intended behavior is unresolved, so the oracle cannot yet distinguish the intended fix from either wrong variant without an operator decision.

The ohosTest cases contain no expect() assertions and only click by text with null guards; whether the UiTest driver reliably finds scrolled-off buttons across the fixed swipe coordinates (400,1200)-(400,400) on different 2in1 screens is unknown, so observables tied to later-button clicks may not be reproducible without hardware qualification.

The project was never built or executed in this analysis; compilation against the API 26 SDK, exposure of the serial namespace by @kit.BasicServicesKit, and availability of a real or virtual serial port on the qualification device are all unverified, and no loopback peer behavior for onDataRead has been specified.
mechanism: State/lifecycle boundary in Index.ets: the single member `port` is assigned only by testGetSerialPortList() and nulled only by testClose(); the other fifteen async handlers each guard on `!this.port` with the '[SerialSample]' log and deliberately keep the port open between operations, while README usage steps 3-12 claim each operation 'auto-closes' the port. Any change toward the documented auto-close behavior mutates a cross-handler state machine: closing-and-nulling inside each handler makes later clicks in the sequence fall into the no-port guard, closing without nulling leaves dangling closed SerialPort objects that fail on subsequent SDK calls, and the ohosTest suite in Ability.test.ets compounds this because it drives buttons strictly by visible text (ON.text) in a fixed order with null-guarded findComponent results that can pass vacuously. The edit must additionally preserve the [Start]/[End] doc-snippet markers around every SDK call, since this tree exists to feed documentation snippets.

observables: The ohosTest suite in Ability.test.ets finds and clicks every button by its unchanged visible text (no vacuous null findComponent skips), and hilog output shows the '[SerialSample]' success log for each operation in the documented order, e.g. 'open success' preceding 'write success, length: ...'.

After a close click, the next data-transfer or signal click logs the '[SerialSample]' guard error 'No serial port found, please call getSerialPortList first' rather than a BusinessError SDK code, and a following getSerialPortList click re-establishes the port so a subsequent operation logs success again.

The [Start]/[End] doc-snippet marker pairs around each SDK call (getSerialPortList, open, write, onDataRead, offDataRead, flush, drain, setRts, getCts, setDtr, getDsr, sendBrk, onDisconnect, offDisconnect, close) remain intact in Index.ets after the edit.
requiredEnvironment: DevEco Studio 7.0 with API 26 SDK (compatibleSdkVersion 26.0.0) and hvigor toolchain able to build Serial/SerialManagerSample/build-profile.json5.
A 2in1 device or emulator running the 7.0 image with a USB virtual serial device or onboard serial attached, so serial.getSerialPortList() returns at least one port.
wrongVariants: Auto-closing and nulling this.port inside every operation handler per a literal reading of README steps 3-12: the subsequent write/onDataRead/flush... clicks in the recorded UiTest order then hit the !port guard and log guard errors instead of success lines, exposing the broken sequential contract.

Closing the port in each handler but leaving this.port non-null: later handlers invoke SDK methods on an already-closed SerialPort, producing BusinessError codes in hilog instead of '[SerialSample]' success messages, and testClose reports success for a port that is not actually open.

Renaming or localizing button labels (or wrapping them in containers that change the ON.text match) so driver.findComponent returns null and the null-guarded click blocks silently no-op: the hypium cases still report 'Pass' while exercising nothing, a vacuous-pass variant that must not count as success.

Dropping or renaming [Start]/[End] marker pairs while restructuring handlers for auto-close: the code may behave correctly but the documentation-snippet extraction contract of the sample tree is violated.

stagedDemands: Align each operation handler with the README-documented open-operate-auto-close flow (e.g. open before write/onDataRead/flush/drain/setRts/getCts/sendBrk, close after), so that clicking any button in isolation performs its full documented lifecycle and logs the '[SerialSample]' success line.

Keep the sequential demo behavior working: after the close button is pressed the shared state is released, subsequent clicks log the 'No serial port found, please call getSerialPortList first' guard instead of SDK error codes, and a new getSerialPortList click restores the port so later operations still succeed.

Preserve the observable contract of the sample: every button keeps its exact visible label (getSerialPortList, portInfo, open, write, onDataRead, offDataRead, flush, drain, setRts, getCts, setDtr, getDsr, sendBrk, close, onDisconnect, offDisconnect) so the UiTest driver can still find and click each one, and every [Start]/[End] snippet marker pair in Index.ets survives the edit.
title: Serial-port demo: per-operation auto-close lifecycle that keeps shared port state, UiTest button driving, and doc-snippet markers consistent

limitations: The end-to-end restore path is not proved in code: the value read from want.parameters['myData'] in onCreate is stored in an unused local, and Index.ets holds only a static 'Hello World'/'Welcome' toggle with no logic to rebuild page state from restored data, so the README's claim that page stack and onSaveState data are recovered is not demonstrated by this checkout.

No build, deploy, emulator, or device execution was performed; the README's stated constraints (RK3568, DevEco Studio version, API level) and its backup-retention claims are unverified doc statements.

The ohosTest entry only asserts that a cold startAbility launch reaches the top; it does not exercise setRestoreEnabled, onSaveState, kill-and-relaunch recovery, or the restored Want parameter, so the sample's recovery behavior has no executable Oracle coverage in this checkout.

Retention claims in README_zh.md (7-day backup storage, 200KB Want serialization limit, no restore across device reboot) are platform behaviors asserted by documentation only; nothing in the checked-in files proves them.

module.json5, backup_config.json, EntryBackupAbility.ets, and the remaining test/list files are pinned from the prior verified fact at the same HEAD revision (blob OIDs re-checked via git rev-parse); only the three refreshed evidence blobs were re-derived this round.
'myData' appears only in EntryAbility.ets; no other tracked file under Ability/UIAbilityRecover references the restored key, so any consumer must be introduced within these files.
mechanism: Cross-lifecycle state-recovery boundary in the UIAbilityRecover leaf: the restore contract is a four-link chain — module.json5 registers the backup extensionAbility with $profile:backup_config, backup_config.json sets allowToBackupRestore:true, onCreate calls this.context.setRestoreEnabled(true) inside try/catch, and onSaveState writes wantParam['myData']='my1234567' and returns AbilityConstant.OnSaveResult.ALL_AGREE. The tested difficulty is that the chain's consumption end is broken by design: onCreate reads want.parameters['myData'] into an unused local (recoveryMyData) and never propagates it, so an abnormal kill followed by relaunch (launchReason APP_RECOVERY carrying the saved Want parameter) is indistinguishable from a cold start in the UI. A correct edit must (a) keep the wiring links intact, and (b) route the restored Want parameter from onCreate into the app's initial visible state without hardcoding the value, while a normal (non-abnormal) exit must still start fresh. The stage-B demand (restore reflects the last interaction, not a constant) is what exposes the cheap stage-A shortcut of hardcoding the recovered string.

observables: ohosTest stage-B scenario: start ability, tap the Text (id 'HelloWorld') to change the visible state, background the app, force-stop the process (hdc shell aa force-stop <bundle>), relaunch via delegator.startAbility, and assert the relaunched page shows the changed state — i.e., EntryAbility restored the exact value previously written by onSaveState into want.parameters['myData'] instead of the cold-start default 'Hello World'.

ohosTest stage-A/scenario wiring check: after the abnormal kill and relaunch, EntryAbility.onCreate observes launchParam.launchReason equal to AbilityConstant.LaunchReason.APP_RECOVERY and want.parameters containing the saved 'myData' entry, and setRestoreEnabled(true) completed without hitting its catch-branch error hilog on the launch preceding the kill.

ohosTest negative-path check: after a normal exit and fresh launch (no abnormal termination), the app starts in its default state and onCreate does not take the APP_RECOVERY restore path, proving restore is bound to abnormal-exit recovery rather than to every launch.
requiredEnvironment: HarmonyOS emulator only, no physical device fallback and no USB/serial/external hardware: a HarmonyOS 6.0.2 (API 22, matching targetSdkVersion 6.0.2(22) in build-profile.json5) phone emulator image of device type 'default' (as listed in module.json5 deviceTypes) managed by DevEco Studio/hvigor, with hdc-over-network access to the emulator for aa force-stop / bundle diagnostics; README_zh.md's RK3568-only note must be overridden by the emulator operator policy.
wrongVariants: Hardcoded-restore variant: onCreate (or the page state it feeds) substitutes a constant string such as 'my1234567' instead of reading want.parameters['myData'] — this passes a plain kill/relaunch check with the stock constant but fails stage B, where the state was changed before the kill and the relaunched page still shows the stale constant.

Wrong-lifecycle persistence variant: state is saved in onDestroy/onBackground into AppStorage or preferences (or onSaveState is left unimplemented/not returning ALL_AGREE) so recovery relies on normal-exit persistence; after an abnormal force-stop the saved data is gone and the relaunch shows the default state, and normal exits get misclassified as restore launches.

Broken-wiring variant: setRestoreEnabled(true) is dropped or moved after the restore consumption (or the module.json5 backup extensionAbilities metadata / allowToBackupRestore:true pairing is removed), so the platform never records the backup and every relaunch — including after force-stop — is a cold start with 'Hello World'.

stagedDemands: Stage A: after the app process is abnormally terminated in the background (e.g., hdc shell aa force-stop) and relaunched, EntryAbility must consume the value restored into want.parameters['myData'] and make it the app's initial visible state, so the relaunched app presents the saved state instead of the cold-start 'Hello World' (the current unused local recoveryMyData must be eliminated).

Stage B: the state handed to onSaveState (returning ALL_AGREE) must reflect the user's latest interaction — e.g., the on-screen message after tapping to change it — so a kill/relaunch performed after changing the state restores the changed state, not a fixed constant.

Stage C: the restore wiring must stay coherent end to end: setRestoreEnabled(true) is still attempted before any restore consumption in onCreate, the module.json5 backup extensionAbilities entry (name/srcEntry/type/metadata $profile:backup_config) and backup_config.json allowToBackupRestore:true are preserved, and a normal foreground close produces a fresh launch (default state) rather than being misread as a restore launch.
title: UIAbility backup-and-restore: make abnormal-exit relaunch recover onSaveState state

limitations: No build, signing, install, or test run was performed: hvigor assembly of the eight products/wearable targets, resolution of the pinned file: dependencies (@ohos/common, devpractices, commonbusiness), and installation of the wearable entry HAP plus ohosTest bundle on the wearable emulator image are all unproven.

The mock dataset behind TriggerEnums.WEARABLE_SAMPLE_TRIGGER was read as source only, so which list item carries isSourceCode=true and its exact title/QR URL used by the stage-2 tap observable are inferred, not verified at runtime, and async QRCode generation timing on the emulator is unknown.

Emulator input fidelity for the stage-3 observable is unresolved: ArcSwiper.onDigitalCrown and onBackPressed behavior may differ without physical crown hardware, and whether ohosTest uiInput can reliably background and re-foreground the ability on a wearable image has not been exercised.
mechanism: Cross-file startup/navigation lockstep of the wearable entry HAP: module.json5 declares entry-type WearableAbility (entity.system.home intent, srcEntry ./ets/wearableability/WearableAbility.ets) and its pages ($profile:main_pages declares pages/SplashPage, $profile:router_map declares the NavDestination map). WearableAbility.onWindowStageCreate must seed AppStorage 'pageContext' with a fresh PageContext (and 'UI_CONTEXT' in the loadContent callback) before SplashPage's @StorageLink('pageContext') reads it; SplashViewModel then replacePage({routerName: PageEnum.MAIN_PAGE}), which resolves only if router_map.json contains a 'MainPage' entry whose pageSourceFile and buildFunction (MainPageBuilder in MainPage.ets) are consistent with the common PageEnum.MAIN_PAGE literal, and SampleListViewModel.jumpToSourceCodeLinkPage openPage({routerName: PageEnum.WEARABLE_SOURCE_CODE_VIEW}) resolves only via the matching 'WearableSourceCodeView' router_map entry. All of these names live in different files (two of them outside the editable scope in @ohos/common), so a drift such as a renamed router_map entry, a mismatched buildFunction, or a re-ordered AppStorage seeding still compiles cleanly and is exposed only at runtime by later-stage user-visible behavior (list render, QR destination push, back-to-background).

observables: After cold launch on the wearable emulator, an ohosTest driver observes the SplashPage Navigation stack settle with a top NavDestination whose name is 'MainPage' within a bounded timeout, and the ArcList contains mock sample items with the sample-library header rendered.

When the driver taps the list item flagged as source code, a NavDestination named 'WearableSourceCodeView' is pushed, its title text equals the tapped item's title and a QRCode component is present; a system back event then returns the stack to 'MainPage' with the list still populated.

When the driver injects a back event on the 'MainPage' root, WearableAbility moves to background (process remains visible to hdc shell, window can be re-foregrounded) and a subsequent foreground/relaunch lands again on 'MainPage' via the splash replace flow rather than showing a blank stack.
requiredEnvironment: DevEco Studio Device Manager HarmonyOS wearable emulator image (device type 'wearable', API 12+ HarmonyOS NEXT wearable system image) running locally as the only test target

hdc connection to that emulator for installing the wearable entry HAP and the ohosTest bundle and for injecting uiInput tap/back events; no physical device, USB, serial, or other attached external hardware
wrongVariants: router_map.json 'MainPage' entry is renamed or repointed (pageSourceFile/buildFunction no longer matching MainPageBuilder): the project builds and the splash background shows, but replacePage resolves no builder, MainPage never renders, and the emulator shows only the splash/black screen with an empty NavPathStack, failing the stage-1 observable.

WearableAbility stops seeding AppStorage 'pageContext' before loadContent (or SplashPage silently falls back to a fresh PageContext): the initial landing still appears, but the pushed WearableSourceCodeView targets a detached NavPathStack, so the QR destination never mounts or back returns to a dead root, exposing the startup-order mistake only at the stage-2 observable.

module.json5 entry skill/srcEntry drift (home intent removed or srcEntry path changed without a matching file): the entry ability no longer launches as the home intent on the emulator, so the ohosTest driver cannot reach SplashPage at all and every later-stage observable fails.

stagedDemands: On wearable emulator launch, the entry ability must show the splash background and then, within a bounded time, replace to the MainPage destination whose ArcList is populated from mock sample data with the sample-library header visible.

Selecting the source-code-flagged sample item must push the WearableSourceCodeView destination showing the tapped item's title and a QR code, and system back must return to the MainPage list without dropping the stack.

Back pressed while on the MainPage root must background WearableAbility (process stays alive and re-foregroundable) instead of popping the Navigation stack or terminating the app, and repeated launch cycles must still land on MainPage from splash.
title: Wearable entry HAP splash-to-main router lockstep under staged navigation demands
